Description:
All three protein(LAF-1 RGG, LAF-1 RGG(2), LAF-1 RGG(3)) solutions exhibited UCST phase behavior—they were transparent at elevated temperatures, but upon cooling they phase separated and become visibly turbid—but their transition temperatures differed significantly depending on the number of RGG repeats.
LAF-1 RGG was miscible at room temperature and phase separated only when the temperature was reduced below 15℃.
LAF-1 RGG(2) phase separated at room temperature and even at physiological temperatures for tissue culture. It was miscible only at temperatures above approximately 40℃. The temperature-dependent phase behavior of RGG-RGG can be cycled; turbidity appeared, disappeared, and then reappeared upon cooling, heating, and recooling.
LAF-1 RGG phase separated even more readily, becoming turbid at temperatures below approximately 50℃.

Description:
Titration of the purified VRN1 with dsDNA FLC55 (55 base pairs (bp) upstream of the FLC promoter) led to the formation of spherical liquid-like droplets, which underwent fusion in a few seconds.
At a given protein concentration, the numbers and sizes of these droplets depended on the DNA concentration.
The labeled VRN1 and FLC55 DNA formed droplets in a similar way as the unlabeled sample. VRN1 and FLC55 colocalized in the droplets with a Pearson's correlation coefficient of 0.98.
The results of fluorescence recovery after bleaching (FRAP) showed that both VRN1 and FLC55 fluorescence recovered rapidly with similar speeds after photobleaching. Bleaching a section of the droplet gave similar results. This indicates the rapid exchange of VRN1 and FLC55 DNA molecules inside and outside the droplets, and shows that the droplets have liquid-like properties.

GFP–PrLD was found to undergo phase separation at 1 μM, and the distinct droplets were spherical. FRAP analysis indicated that GFP–PrLD molecules diffused rapidly within droplets, and exchanged between droplets and surrounding solution. Droplets were found to fuse upon contact. These data collectively indicate that GFP–PrLD undergoes liquid–liquid phase separation. However, the puncta formed by GFP–FCA in vitro did not show similar liquidity.

Description:
To observe the phase separation of hnRNPA1, we cooled down the hnRNPA1 solution from 25℃ to 4℃. The solution turned cloudy in a few minutes. Differential interference contrast (DIC) microscopy showed spherical droplets of hnRNPA1 in the liquid phase. The liquid property of the droplets was shown as that two adjacent droplets fused spontaneously within seconds measured by optical tweezers. 
By negative-staining TEM, we observed bunches of amyloid fibrils in the droplets. We further validated the amyloid fibril formation by monitoring Thioflavin T (ThT) fluorescence using confocal microscopy and spectrophotometry. The results showed a specific enhancement of ThT intensity in the droplets, which consistent with the TEM imaging, indicates amyloid fibril formation in the droplets. 
As temperature reverted back to 25℃, the hnRNPA1 solution became clear again, and neither droplet nor amyloid fibril was observed, indicating that the fibrils are reversible. As we estimated based on the ThT intensity, <10% of the total proteins in molecules formed reversible fibrils. Moreover, as we kept the cloudy hnRNPA1 solution at 4℃ for hours, the solution spontaneously became clear and the amount of reversible fibrils decreased accordingly. Overnight, a significant amount of irreversible amyloid fibrils emerged which are stable as temperature increased to 25℃ for elongated time. 
In these experiments, we observed three states of hnRNPA1 assemblies: liquid-like droplets, reversible fibrils, and irreversible fibrils.

This turbidity increase was clearly detectable at a protein concentration as low as 2 µM. Importantly, under all conditions tested, the effect showed a strong dependence on the ionic strength of the buffer, with higher amounts of PEG required to induce LLPS in the presence of increasing concentrations of NaCl.

Description: The propensity of ∆2N tau to undergo LLPS was diminished, as indicated by lower turbidity and requirement for higher concentrations of the crowding agent as compared to that for tau441. However, droplets still could be observed for this variant by microscopy, especially at higherconcentrations of PEG. Building on this finding, next we performed experiments with the N-truncated variant tau ∆1-117, in which the entire negatively charged segment has been removed. This deletion resulted in an essentially complete loss of ability to undergo LLPS, further reinforcing our central hypothesis regarding the crucial role of intermolecular electrostatic interactions between oppositely charged regions of tau. Consistent with this notion, no phase separation was observed for the negatively charged N-terminal fragment (tau ∆118-441) alone. Deletion of the entire four-repeat (4R) region (residues 244-369) modestly decreased the propensity of tau to undergo LLPS, as indicated by reduced sample turbidity, but droplets still could be observed by microscopy. This suggests that the repeats, a region critical for pathological aggregation of tau, are not essential for LLPS. Most C-terminal 402-441 segment that is predominantly negatively charged (especially within residues 418-434) appears to play a minor role, as deletion of this entire segment (tau∆402-441) had little effect on LLPS.

Description: The ThT fluorescence curves shown in Fig. 3 demonstrate that, for all tau441 variants studied, LLPS results in a dramatic acceleration of the fibrillation reaction. In sharp contrast, no measurable increase in ThT fluorescence intensity was observed up to at least 40 h for the reaction in the absence of LLPS. Description:
Titration of the purified VRN1 with dsDNA FLC55 (55 base pairs (bp) upstream of the FLC promoter) led to the formation of spherical liquid-like droplets, which underwent fusion in a few seconds.
At a given protein concentration, the numbers and sizes of these droplets depended on the DNA concentration.
The labeled VRN1 and FLC55 DNA formed droplets in a similar way as the unlabeled sample. VRN1 and FLC55 colocalized in the droplets with a Pearson's correlation coefficient of 0.98.
The results of fluorescence recovery after bleaching (FRAP) showed that both VRN1 and FLC55 fluorescence recovered rapidly with similar speeds after photobleaching. Bleaching a section of the droplet gave similar results. This indicates the rapid exchange of VRN1 and FLC55 DNA molecules inside and outside the droplets, and shows that the droplets have liquid-like properties.

Description:
To observe the phase separation of hnRNPA1, we cooled down the hnRNPA1 solution from 25℃ to 4℃. The solution turned cloudy in a few minutes. Differential interference contrast (DIC) microscopy showed spherical droplets of hnRNPA1 in the liquid phase. The liquid property of the droplets was shown as that two adjacent droplets fused spontaneously within seconds measured by optical tweezers. 
By negative-staining TEM, we observed bunches of amyloid fibrils in the droplets. We further validated the amyloid fibril formation by monitoring Thioflavin T (ThT) fluorescence using confocal microscopy and spectrophotometry. The results showed a specific enhancement of ThT intensity in the droplets, which consistent with the TEM imaging, indicates amyloid fibril formation in the droplets. 
As temperature reverted back to 25℃, the hnRNPA1 solution became clear again, and neither droplet nor amyloid fibril was observed, indicating that the fibrils are reversible. As we estimated based on the ThT intensity, <10% of the total proteins in molecules formed reversible fibrils. Moreover, as we kept the cloudy hnRNPA1 solution at 4℃ for hours, the solution spontaneously became clear and the amount of reversible fibrils decreased accordingly. Overnight, a significant amount of irreversible amyloid fibrils emerged which are stable as temperature increased to 25℃ for elongated time. 
In these experiments, we observed three states of hnRNPA1 assemblies: liquid-like droplets, reversible fibrils, and irreversible fibrils.

Description: The propensity of ∆2N tau to undergo LLPS was diminished, as indicated by lower turbidity and requirement for higher concentrations of the crowding agent as compared to that for tau441. However, droplets still could be observed for this variant by microscopy, especially at higherconcentrations of PEG. Building on this finding, next we performed experiments with the N-truncated variant tau ∆1-117, in which the entire negatively charged segment has been removed. This deletion resulted in an essentially complete loss of ability to undergo LLPS, further reinforcing our central hypothesis regarding the crucial role of intermolecular electrostatic interactions between oppositely charged regions of tau. Consistent with this notion, no phase separation was observed for the negatively charged N-terminal fragment (tau ∆118-441) alone. Deletion of the entire four-repeat (4R) region (residues 244-369) modestly decreased the propensity of tau to undergo LLPS, as indicated by reduced sample turbidity, but droplets still could be observed by microscopy. This suggests that the repeats, a region critical for pathological aggregation of tau, are not essential for LLPS. Most C-terminal 402-441 segment that is predominantly negatively charged (especially within residues 418-434) appears to play a minor role, as deletion of this entire segment (tau∆402-441) had little effect on LLPS.

Description: The ThT fluorescence curves shown in Fig. 3 demonstrate that, for all tau441 variants studied, LLPS results in a dramatic acceleration of the fibrillation reaction. For the wild-type protein, the lag phase of the reaction under LLPS conditions was ~16 h. In sharp contrast, no measurable increase in ThT fluorescence intensity was observed up to at least 40 h for the reaction in the absence of LLPS. This effect was even stronger for the mutant proteins . For example, for the P301L variant, the lag phase was reduced from ~17 h in the absence of LLPS to ~3 h in the droplet environment, and the rate of the growth phase was also greatly increased. The rate of fibrillation under LLPS conditions was especially high for the ΔK280 variant. In the latter case, the reaction (without any measurable lag phase) was essentially completed within 30 min, in sharp contrast to the lack of any ThT fluorescence increase up to at least 40 h in the absence of LLPS. The final ThT intensities at the end of the growth phase under LLPS conditions were different for individual tau variants.Importantly, consistent with the ThT data, no fibrillar structures were observed in AFM images for individual proteins at the same time points under the conditions of no LLPS.
